docRequirement: A channel server pushes events with the JSON-RPC notification method `notifications/claude/channel`, whose params are `content` (string, the event body) and optional `meta` (`Record<string, string>`, each entry becoming an attribute on the `<channel>` tag; keys must be identifiers of letters, digits and underscores only, other keys are silently dropped) — channels-reference.md:48, :221, :225, :229-230. The bare string `claude/channel` is a DIFFERENT thing on that page: it is only the capability key `capabilities.experimental['claude/channel']` (:198, :212), whose presence is what registers the listener.
current: We listen on the capability key as if it were the method, and read a param name that does not exist in the contract. `packages/shared/src/mcp/client.ts:112-114` declares `const ClaudeChannelNotificationSchema = NotificationSchema.extend({ method: z.literal('claude/channel') })` — no `notifications/` prefix. `packages/shared/src/mcp/client.ts:357-361` registers it and reads `const text = (notification.params as { text?: unknown } | undefined)?.text`, returning early unless `typeof text === 'string'`; `meta` is never read. The in-process message type has no room for it: `packages/shared/src/mcp/client.ts:102-105` is `interface McpChannelMessage { server: string; text: string }`, and the pool's ingress guard `packages/shared/src/mcp/mcp-pool.ts:370-376` requires `typeof message.text === 'string'` within `MCP_CHANNEL_MAX_TEXT_BYTES` (client.ts:173, 32 KiB, sanitized by `boundedChannelText` at client.ts:175-188). Dispatch is by exact method string with no escape hatch: `node_modules/@modelcontextprotocol/sdk/dist/esm/shared/protocol.js:913-919` registers under `getMethodLiteral(schema)` and `:273-277` does `this._notificationHandlers.get(notification.method) ?? this.fallbackNotificationHandler` then `if (handler === undefined) return;` ('Ignore notifications not being subscribed to'); `grep -arn 'fallbackNotificationHandler' packages apps --include='*.ts'` (NUL-safe) returns 0 hits, so nothing catches the unmatched method. Every sibling notification in the same constructor does carry the prefix (`ToolListChangedNotificationSchema` etc., client.ts:349-356 = `notifications/tools/list_changed`), which is what marks this as a rename miss rather than a house style. `grep -arn 'notifications/claude' --exclude-dir=node_modules --exclude-dir=.git --exclude-dir=.references .` matches only sweep documents under docs/, never source. Downstream the rest of the path is built and works: `setChannelHandler` (client.ts:672-674) -> `applyChannelPolicy` (mcp-pool.ts:758-771) -> `dispatchChannelMessage` (mcp-pool.ts:1082-1106) -> `subscribeChannel` (mcp-pool.ts:714-722) -> `packages/server-core/src/sessions/SessionManager.ts:2435-2439`, which destructures `({ text })` and calls `canDeliver()?.redirect(text)`. The gate is fail-closed: `ChannelPolicy`/`CHANNEL_PUSH_OFF` (mcp-pool.ts:341, :361, :632-633) and `mcpChannelPushEnabled` default `false` (`packages/shared/src/config/storage.ts:95`, `:183`, resolved at `:1142-1155`), with the managed lock `channelsEnabled` (`packages/shared/src/agent/pi-harness/managed-policy.ts:230`, `:515`, `:1317-1318`).
divergence: Two wrong strings on the ingress, plus one field that has nowhere to go. (1) The registered method literal is `claude/channel` where the contract says `notifications/claude/channel` — the value we used is real, but it is the capability key, not the method, so the prefix is simply missing. (2) The param read is `params.text` where the contract says `params.content` — again only the key name is wrong; the value's meaning, sanitization and 32 KiB bound are all correct and can be kept as-is. (3) `meta` is absent at the type level, not merely unread: `McpChannelMessage` carries no field for it and the pool guard would reject nothing but also preserve nothing. Because MCP dispatch is an exact string map with no fallback handler here, (1) alone means a doc-conforming channel server has every event dropped with no error and no log; (2) means even a server that used our un-prefixed method would still be ignored unless it happened to send `text`. Nothing in the repo emits either form (`grep -arn 'claude/channel'` over source finds only client.ts:113 plus prose in docs-site), so there is no in-house producer to stay compatible with.

change.what: One-line literal fix: `method: z.literal('notifications/claude/channel')`. The SDK's `NotificationSchema` has `params: NotificationsParamsSchema.loose().optional()` (node_modules/@modelcontextprotocol/sdk/dist/esm/types.js:96-99), so `content`/`meta` pass through the parse untouched and no schema shape change is needed. Optionally keep a second constant `LegacyClaudeChannelNotificationSchema` on the old un-prefixed literal and register it too, but note no shipped server emits it — dropping it is the cleaner default.

Read `content` instead of `text`: `const content = (notification.params as { content?: unknown; text?: unknown } | undefined)?.content`, keeping the existing `typeof !== 'string'` guard, the `this.channelServer` guard and `boundedChannelText(...)` unchanged. Accept `params.text` only as a tolerated fallback if the legacy schema above is retained. Add `meta` extraction next to it: keep only own enumerable entries whose key matches `/^[A-Za-z0-9_]+$/` and whose value is a string (the page's 'Keys must be identifiers … silently dropped' rule), sanitize values through the same `INVALID_CHANNEL_CONTROL` strip as the body, and bound the collected size so a hostile server cannot bypass `MCP_CHANNEL_MAX_TEXT_BYTES` via attributes. Emit `this.channelHandler?.({ server, text: boundedChannelText(content), meta })` with `meta` omitted when empty.

Add `meta?: Record<string, string>`. Keep the field named `text` internally — the doc constrains the wire key, not our in-process name, and renaming it would touch all 10 callers for no contract gain.

Accept the new optional field: when `message.meta !== undefined` it must be a plain object whose every value is a string and whose every key matches the identifier rule, otherwise reject the message (or drop just `meta`, matching whichever the client-side filter chose — pick one and state it in the comment). Existing `server`/`text`/byte-bound checks stay.

change.symbol: 'emits only bounded sanitized text from claude/channel notifications' (:110-135)
change.what: This test currently PINS the bug: `handlers.get('claude/channel')!` at :117 and `params: { text: … }` at :121-131. Retarget to `handlers.get('notifications/claude/channel')`, send `content`, and keep the existing NUL/ESC-strip, non-string-rejection and 32 KiB-truncation assertions. Add two cases: a `meta` with one identifier key and one hyphenated key, asserting the hyphenated one is dropped; and (if the legacy alias is not retained) an assertion that no handler is registered for the bare `claude/channel` string.

Prose says `claude/channel` where it means the notification. Reword to name the method `notifications/claude/channel` (the capability key keeps its own name). Mirror in docs-site/content/ru/sources/mcp-servers/overview.md:14, docs-site/content/plugins/overview.md:26 and docs-site/content/ru/plugins/overview.md:26.

blastRadius: Crosses a WIRE boundary — the JSON-RPC method string and param names we accept from third-party MCP servers — which is an explicit risk trigger in this repo, so the expanded check should run once on the final diff. No persistence or protocol-DTO change: `meta` stops at the in-memory `McpChannelMessage` and is not serialized anywhere today. Internal readers of the changed symbols: `NessyMcpClient.setChannelHandler` (packages/shared/src/mcp/client.ts:279, :672) -> `McpClientPool.applyChannelPolicy` (mcp-pool.ts:758-771, also called on register at :1063-1064) -> `dispatchChannelMessage` (:1082-1106, guarded by `isMcpChannelMessage`) -> `subscribeChannel` (:714-722) -> `SessionManager.ts:2435-2439`, then `PiAgent.redirect` as a `steer` message. `McpChannelMessage` has 10 callers across mcp-pool.ts and client.ts (codegraph blast radius). Tests that touch this area: packages/shared/src/mcp/__tests__/client-transport.test.ts:110-135 (the only one that asserts the wire literal, and it must change), packages/shared/tests/mcp-pool.test.ts:684-727 and packages/server-core/src/sessions/__tests__/mcp-channel-gate.test.ts:10-104 and packages/server-core/src/sessions/SessionManager.process-supervisor.test.ts:981 — those three inject at the `PoolClient.emitChannel({ server, text })` seam, so the method rename does not disturb them, but a widened `McpChannelMessage` may need one `meta` case. Config surfaces are untouched: `mcpChannelPushEnabled` (packages/shared/src/config/storage.ts:95, :183, :1142-1155, :1209; packages/shared/src/config/validators.ts:121, :171; config-defaults-schema.ts:33-35) and managed `channelsEnabled` (managed-policy.ts:230, :515, :1317) keep their names and defaults. Two adjacent rows this fix does NOT close and must not be conflated with: f136 (wrapping the event in a `<channel source=…>` tag with `meta` as attributes — the reason `meta` must be plumbed here even though nothing consumes it yet) and f137 (the `notifications/claude/channel/permission_request` / `…/permission` relay half, absent entirely). Separately unverified against the doc and out of scope: we arm the dispatcher from policy alone and never inspect the server's advertised `capabilities.experimental['claude/channel']`, which is more permissive than the page's 'Presence registers the notification listener'.
userImpact: None observable today, because channel push is fail-closed: `mcpChannelPushEnabled` defaults to `false` (packages/shared/src/config/storage.ts:183) and `CHANNEL_PUSH_OFF` (mcp-pool.ts:361) installs no dispatcher, so no shipped configuration can reach the handler. It surfaces the moment a user turns channel push on and connects any channel server written from Claude's page — the Telegram/Slack/CI bridges the page itself walks through. Then: the server connects fine, the source shows healthy, the bridge reports it posted the event, and the session never reacts. Every notification is discarded inside the MCP SDK's unmatched-method branch, so there is no error toast, no source-health degradation and no debug line to explain it; from the user's side the feature is simply inert. The only way to make it work today is to hand-patch the third-party server to emit `claude/channel` with a `text` param, i.e. to write against a contract nobody documents.
